statements.quote: In a Transformer, words are processed in parallel.

Without **Positional Encoding (PE)**, the model would treat the sentence *“The dog bit the man”* exactly the same as *“The man bit the dog”* (and also the same as *“dog the The man bit”* and all other combinations of these words).
To fix this, we **add** a unique mathematical “signature” to each word's vector based on its position ($\text{pos}$), with on sine and cosine.
The challenge of processing text in parallel (instead of word-by-word like older RNNs) required a new way to inject “time” or “order” into the model.
statements.section: The Invention of the Transformer & Positional Encoding

statements.quote: * **The “\citetitle{vaswani2017attention}” Paper:** This landmark work by Vaswani et al. replaced sequential processing with the Transformer architecture.
statements.section: The Invention of the Transformer & Positional Encoding

statements.quote: Since Transformers have no inherent sense of order, the authors introduced **Sinusoidal Positional Encodings**.
statements.section: The Invention of the Transformer & Positional Encoding

statements.quote: * **Why Waves?** The researchers chose alternating sine and cosine functions because they allow the model to attend to relative positions.
statements.section: The Invention of the Transformer & Positional Encoding

statements.quote: The different frequencies, ranging from “fast” wiggles to “slow” curves, act like a multi-scale clock, marking every position in a sequence with a unique, bounded mathematical signature.
statements.section: The Invention of the Transformer & Positional Encoding

statements.quote: Vaswani et al. chose the base 10000 so that the wavelengths form a geometric progression: the slowest pair completes one cycle every $10000\cdot 2\pi$ positions, and each faster pair is a fixed factor quicker.
statements.section: The Invention of the Transformer & Positional Encoding

statements.quote: The paper's motivation was not only uniqueness but linearity: for any fixed offset $k$, $PE_{pos+k}$ is a fixed linear function of $PE_{pos}$, so attention can learn relative distance without a lookup table (\cite{vaswani2017attention}).
statements.section: The Invention of the Transformer & Positional Encoding

statements.quote: **Adjacent positions are close together.** Neighboring points sit right next to each other on the curve.
statements.section: Positional Encoding Creates a Manifold, Not Just Labels

statements.quote: **Translational symmetry.** The **blue segment** (pos 5 to 8) and the **red segment** (pos 105 to 108) have the **same length** (equal chords of the helix), even though each points in a different direction as the helix turns.

statements.quote: A fixed offset $k$ corresponds to a fixed rotation matrix $M_k$ independent of absolute position, just like a clock face lets you compute “3 hours from now” regardless of what time it currently is.

statements.quote: **Generalization to unseen lengths.** The encoding is defined for every integer position, and its geometry makes “nearby” vs “far away” explicit.

statements.quote: Recall the rotation matrix for each sine-cosine pair at frequency $\omega$:
statements.section: The PE Rotation Group

statements.quote: The set $\{M_k : k \in \mathbb{R}\}$ satisfies all four axioms of a **group** — closure, associativity, an identity ($M_0 = I$), and an inverse ($M_{-k}$) — so it is the **circle group** $SO(2)$, the group of all 2D rotations.
statements.section: The PE Rotation Group

statements.quote: (For the full four-axiom treatment and the history of the group concept, see the Basic Math IV lesson.) Since a full PE vector is a stack of independent sine-cosine pairs at different frequencies, the complete positional encoding lives in a **product of circle groups, a torus**.
statements.section: The PE Rotation Group

statements.quote: The helix above is not the torus itself; it is a one-dimensional curve wound around it, tracing how a single position moves as the index increases.
statements.section: The PE Rotation Group

statements.quote: **“3 apart” is always the same $M_3$**, whether you start at position 2 or position 2000.
statements.section: Why the Group Structure Matters for Attention

statements.quote: **Compositions compose predictably**: “3 forward, then 5 forward” equals “8 forward” ($M_3 \cdot M_5 = M_8$).
statements.section: Why the Group Structure Matters for Attention

statements.quote: **Reversibility**: the model can ask “what was 3 positions *before* me?” via $M_{-3}$.
statements.section: Why the Group Structure Matters for Attention

statements.quote: The rotations themselves are fixed by the encoding; the $Q$ and $K$ linear projections learn to read the rotated coordinates.
statements.section: Why the Group Structure Matters for Attention

statements.quote: The group structure is an inductive bias, not a guarantee: an offset that works at one location is represented the same way everywhere, but training still has to discover which offsets matter.
statements.section: Why the Group Structure Matters for Attention

statements.quote: No special circuitry, no lookup tables, just linear algebra riding on top of algebraic symmetry.
statements.section: Why the Group Structure Matters for Attention

statements.quote: **The aha-moment:** Positional encoding doesn't just *label* positions, it gives the model an **algebraic compass** that works identically everywhere in the sequence.
statements.section: Why the Group Structure Matters for Attention

statements.quote: What happens when you repeat the same word hundreds of times in a sequence?
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: The **semantic embedding** is identical every time, but the **positional encoding** nudges each copy to a slightly different point in space.

statements.quote: From it, **hundreds of lines** radiate outward to the final embedding of “king” at each position (0 through 199).
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: The result is a starburst that reveals the geometry of positional encoding itself:
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: - **Short lines** mean the PE at that position barely moved the vector.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: - **The pattern of directions** shows how the sine/cosine waves systematically sweep the word through embedding space.

statements.quote: - **No two endpoints are the same**: Every position is unique, even though the word is identical.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: The need to encode sequential order is as old as neural sequence modeling itself.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: **Recurrent networks** like the \citetitle{lstm} and \citealternativetitle{elman1990finding} encoded position *implicitly*, the hidden state accumulated positional context step by step.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: **Time-Delay Neural Networks** (Waibel et al., 1989) hard-coded local temporal structure through fixed delay windows.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: When convolutional models entered sequence tasks, \cite[Gehring et al.]{gehring2017convs2s} added learned position embeddings to compensate for convolution's shift-invariance, among the earliest *explicit, additive* position embeddings.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: **Sinusoidal encodings (2017).** The \citetitle{vaswani2017attention} faced a new problem: with no recurrence and no convolution, position had to be injected as a pure signal.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: The authors chose fixed sine/cosine functions at geometrically decreasing frequencies.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: Because $PE_{\text{pos}+k}$ is a linear function of $PE_{\text{pos}}$, relative offsets are implicitly representable, no learned parameters required.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: **Learned absolute embeddings (2018–2019).** \citealternativetitle{firstgpt}, \citealternativetitle{bert}, and \citealternativetitle{gpt2} replaced sinusoids with a trainable embedding matrix.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: Simple and effective, but unable to generalize beyond the maximum trained length.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: Learned absolute embeddings are a matrix $E\in\mathbb{R}^{L_{\max}\times d}$ indexed by position and trained end to end.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: BERT used a 512-token table (\cite{bert}); GPT-2 used 1024 (\cite{gpt2}).
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: Each row is a free parameter, so a position beyond $L_{\max}$ has no vector at all: the model cannot even be run, let alone extrapolate.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: That is the trade-off the sinusoids tried to avoid.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: Learned positions fit the training distribution better, but fixed sinusoids at least assign a value to every integer position, however poorly the trained model uses the far ones.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: **Relative position encodings (2018).** Shaw et al. (\citetitle{shaw2018relative}) argued that what matters is the *distance* between tokens, not their absolute index.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: They learned a vector for each clipped relative offset and added it to the key and value representations, extending the dynamic alignment intuition of \citeauthor{bahdanau2014} to position itself.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: T5 later simplified this to a learned per-head bias on the attention logits (\cite{raffel2020t5}).
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: Shaw et al. did not add a bias to the logits.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: They learned a vector for each clipped relative offset and added it to the key and value representations, so the query-key score contains a term $x_iW^Q(a_{ij}^K)^\top$ on top of the usual content match (\cite{shaw2018relative}).
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: T5 simplified the idea: a learned scalar bias per head is added directly to the attention logits, one bias per bucket of relative distance (\cite{raffel2020t5}).
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: In both cases the representation of a distance is independent of where it occurs in the sequence, which is why relative schemes extrapolate better than absolute tables.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: **RoPE (2021).** Su et al. (\citetitle{rope2021}) encode absolute position as a **rotation** in the complex plane applied to query and key vectors.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: Since the dot product of two rotated vectors depends only on the *angle difference*, absolute information naturally yields a relative signal.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: Now the dominant scheme in open-weight LLMs.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: RoPE multiplies query and key vectors by a position-dependent complex rotation.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: Because $q_m^\top k_n$ depends only on $m-n$, the attention score is relative by construction, while the vectors themselves still carry absolute phase (\cite{rope2021}).
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: The scheme is elegant but not automatically length-extrapolating: rotary frequencies are fixed at pre-training, and quality degrades past the trained window.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: Position Interpolation rescales positions to fit the original range (\cite{chen2023position}); YaRN interpolates frequencies and adjusts the attention temperature (\cite{peng2023yarn}).
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: Standard versions of both need a short fine-tuning pass; YaRN's Dynamic Scaling variant can stretch the window without training.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: **ALiBi (2022).** Press et al. (\citetitle{alibi2022}) use no positional embeddings at all, just a fixed **linear penalty** proportional to query-key distance, with a different slope per head.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: Zero learned parameters, strong length extrapolation.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: ALiBi takes the opposite route: it adds no position vector at all.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: Each attention head receives a fixed linear penalty $-m_h\,(i-j)$ on the score for a query at position $i$ and a key at $j\le i$, with a head-specific slope $m_h$; the slopes form a geometric sequence (\cite{alibi2022}).
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: Because the penalty is defined for any distance, a model trained on short sequences can be evaluated on much longer ones, though quality still degrades gradually.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: ALiBi is the cleanest demonstration that relative distance, not absolute index, is what many tasks actually need.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: **Length extension.** Techniques like **Position Interpolation** (\cite{chen2023position}) and **YaRN** (\cite{peng2023yarn}) let models trained on 4K tokens operate over 32K–128K by rescaling or frequency-adjusting existing positional schemes.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions

statements.quote: Position Interpolation needs about 1,000 fine-tuning steps; standard YaRN needs a short fine-tuning pass, though its Dynamic Scaling variant can stretch the window without training.
statements.section: The Repetition Starburst: One Word, Many Positions
